items.text: On Oct 26 a Ninth Circuit panel voted 2-1 to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction the Justice Department's emergency appeal, which sought to make California set aside about 20,000 mail ballots from voters that federal agencies flagged as likely noncitizens. Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez formed the majority. They said DOJ gave the district court only about 15 hours, three of them business hours, to rule on its restraining-order request before calling the delay a 'constructive denial'. They also noted DOJ had known of its concerns for months and sued after ballot processing began. Judge Patrick Bumatay dissented. The merits now go back to US District Judge David O. Carter, whose hearing is set for Oct 27.
items.notes: The opinion PDF was not opened; facts come from FOX 11's account of the opinion. CNN, the Gateway Pundit (right) and Law Commentary headlines agree on the outcome. I found no DOJ or California reaction, and no word yet on whether DOJ will go to the Supreme Court. The Fox News live blog, written before the ruling, still described the appeal as pending. The judge's full name, David O. Carter, comes from earlier coverage of the case reassignment.

items.text: In a late-Sunday (Oct 25) filing, Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign and the DSCC asked US District Judge Sharon Gleason in Alaska to throw out DOJ's suit seeking to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan narrowly loses. They call the suit wholly baseless and an unconstitutional federal intrusion into state election administration, and they asked her to act this week. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on CNN that the suit only seeks to find out whether voter confusion broke the law and that Trump is not trying to take over a state election. No hearing date has been reported.
items.notes: I read the Reuters wire copy but not the court filing. On the right, Fox News's live blog frames it around Republican claims that Democrats boosted the same-name candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., which he denies, and quotes Iowa Democrat Rob Sand criticizing both parties. Sen. Adam Schiff says DOJ lacks standing.

items.text: Eight days before the midterms, Trump held his first Mississippi rally since 2019, in Corinth on Oct 26, for Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith against Democrat Scott Colom. Trump told the crowd he could not take a chance on the race and admitted Republicans could have a rough night. He credited tariffs, deportations and lower crime, while some supporters complained about grocery and gas prices. Most ratings still have the seat Likely Republican. A Democratic-firm poll (Change Research, Oct 21-22) had Hyde-Smith up only 43-40. VP Vance rallied in Belgrade, Montana, and Topeka, Kansas, where Republicans are also playing defense. Fox News reported more than 27.4 million early votes cast by Monday morning, including 4.35 million in Texas. Trump rallies in Lubbock and Corpus Christi, Texas, for Senate nominee Ken Paxton on Oct 27.
items.notes: Mississippi Today, a local nonprofit, stresses Trump's sagging approval, rambling remarks and voters' cost-of-living complaints. Fox frames the day as a broad Republican push and adds DHS charges against five noncitizens for illegal voting and Trump's $1 million reward for election-fraud tips. Newsweek cites the poll and ratings. The early-vote figure is from Fox and was not checked against a tracker.

items.text: CNN, citing two US officials and an Israeli source, reported on Oct 26 that US forces could start a major operation against Iranian military, nuclear and energy targets within 96 hours of a Trump order. Some officials see the period after the Nov 3 midterms as the likeliest window. CNN also reported that Netanyahu pressed for a joint strike before Israel's election, but Trump asked Israel to wait while signalling joint action soon. Netanyahu's office called the report fake news, the White House declined to comment, and the Pentagon said it plans whatever options the President orders. Meanwhile Qatari mediators visited Tehran in an effort coordinated with the US, and Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish security chiefs held talks there. Iran says messages are still passing through intermediaries.
items.reporter: Lazar Berman, Emanuel Fabian (ToI, relaying CNN)
items.outlet: CNN via Times of Israel; CBS News
items.notes: CNN's original article (cnn.com/2026/10/26/politics/us-iran-strike-plans-trump) could not be fetched because of robots rules, so this relies on Times of Israel and IBTimes UK accounts of it. All sources are anonymous, and the Israeli PMO denies it. CBS says a third US carrier group has been sent while the overall US footprint is quietly shrinking. CENTCOM says the blockade has cost Iran at least $25 billion in oil revenue.

items.text: US stocks rose on Oct 26 as the FOMC prepared to open its two-day meeting on Oct 27. The S&P 500 gained 0.70% to 7,676.80, the Nasdaq 0.82% to 26,169.38 and the Dow 0.28% to 52,361.52. Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI trade ahead of earnings from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon. Oil eased on hopes of de-escalation with Iran, with WTI at $101.40 and Brent at $115.20, but both remain far above pre-war levels. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 4.98% and the 2-year about 4.71%. The fed funds target range is 3.75-4.00%, and futures price about a 90% chance of a hold on Oct 28 and about 73% odds of a December hike after September CPI came in at 3.7% year on year.
items.notes: Index closes come from TheStreet; Treasury yields are midday figures. Rate odds come from CME FedWatch as cited by Kiplinger, and TheStreet put hike odds for this meeting at about 10%. The decision is due 2 pm ET Oct 28 (watch W-261026-01).

items.text: Anthropic made its S-1 registration public on Oct 26 for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading 22 banks. The filing shows first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion and a first operating profit in Q2. It also shows an $80.7 billion net loss, driven mostly by a non-cash $72.4 billion revaluation of convertible notes. A co-founder-owned Class F share keeps 50.1% of ordinary voting power, and the Long-Term Benefit Trust can elect a board majority. Price range and share count are blank. The WSJ, citing sources, reported a possible listing the week of Nov 16 raising $100 billion or more at a $1.5-2 trillion valuation.
items.notes: Figures are from TNW's reading of the S-1; I did not open the SEC filing itself. The valuation and timing come from anonymous sources via the WSJ. Disclosure: this desk's research is produced with Anthropic's Claude, so readers may want to treat this item with that in mind.

items.text: EQT and Range Resources announced on Oct 26 an all-stock merger that creates an Appalachian natural-gas producer with a pro forma enterprise value above $50 billion and more than 9 Bcfe/d of net production. Range holders will get 0.987 EQT shares per share and own about 27% of the combined company. Closing is expected in Q1 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. The deal comes as war-driven energy prices stay high.
items.notes: The deal facts come from the company press release (SEC 8-K).

items.text: Reuters, citing two US and four Canadian sources, reported on Oct 26 that Washington and Ottawa are working on a possibly narrow deal to ease Section 232 tariffs on Canadian steel (up to 50%) and autos (25%). Canada is seeking relief for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. A Canadian source said a deal before Nov 3 is possible. Commerce Secretary Lutnick and Canada's Dominic LeBlanc are in regular contact, and LeBlanc's office described a 'constructive dialogue'. Trump told a Michigan rally on Oct 25 the dispute would be resolved soon. Separately, Trump's Oct 23 changes to the Section 338 list take effect Oct 30; they also drop some packaging items, such as corrugated cartons, and add some paper and label products.
items.notes: All sources are anonymous, and the White House, Commerce and USTR did not comment. Trump has previously said steel and auto tariffs on Canada rise to 50% on Jan 1, 2027. I found no CBP guidance or Canadian retaliation for the Oct 30 change.

items.text: The Treasury Department's proposed rules carrying out the COINS Act, passed in the 2026 defense bill, were published in the Federal Register on Oct 26. They would ban or require notification of US investments in semiconductors, quantum, supercomputing, hypersonics and what the draft calls 'super intelligence systems' in China (including Hong Kong and Macau), Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia. Treasury also proposes adding biotechnology. Penalties could reach IEEPA maximums, including forced divestment. Comments are due Dec 7, and a final rule will set the start date.
items.notes: Treasury released the draft on Thursday, Oct 22, and Federal Register publication was Oct 26. EasternHerald and EconoTimes headlines say China objected and reserved the right to respond; I did not read those articles.

items.text: CMS's proposed rule on Exchange pre-eligibility verification (CMS-9873-P) is published in the Federal Register on Oct 27, which starts a 30-day comment period. Exchanges would have to verify income, household size, citizenship or immigration status, other coverage and residence before paying advance premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions. People could still enroll without subsidies while checks are pending, and subsidies would be paid retroactively once eligibility is verified. People auto-re-enrolled would lose subsidies unless they re-verify. The provisions would apply from plan year 2028, with a first verification window opening Aug 1, 2027.
items.notes: Correction to yesterday's item: per the CMS fact sheet, the rule applies to plan year 2028, not the current open enrollment. The exact comment deadline is inferred as about Nov 26 (30 days after publication); I could not open the Federal Register document to confirm it.

items.text: A CDC order signed Oct 22, appearing in the Federal Register on Oct 27, will require every air passenger flying to or connecting through the US to attest that they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the previous 21 days. It applies to flights departing at or after 11:59 pm EST on Nov 3. Airlines must deny boarding to passengers who do not attest and keep the forms for 42 days. False statements can be prosecuted. The order responds to the Central Africa Ebola epidemic, where confirmed deaths have reportedly passed 4,690.
items.notes: The order was announced Oct 22-23, but I could not find it in yesterday's brief, so it is included now that it is formally published. The death toll comes from a travel blog citing outbreak figures and is unverified. This applies to travellers from Poland too.

items.text: India-based Pritam International voluntarily recalled more than 4 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste sold nationwide, after FDA flagged manufacturing 'deviations' at the packaging facility. Affected brands include Brush Buddies children's lines with Hot Wheels, Crayola, My Little Pony and Barbie branding, with expiry dates into 2028. FDA classed it Class II, a moderate risk, and no illnesses have been reported (FDA event #99849).
items.notes: From a local TV report citing the FDA enforcement report. I could not open the FDA recall database to confirm.

items.text: The full Fifth Circuit ruled 10-7 on Oct 23 that immigrants who entered without admission and are held under mandatory detention (INA Section 1225) have no constitutional right to an individualized bond hearing during removal proceedings. The ruling overturns a July panel decision requiring hearings within 90 days. Judge Cory Wilson wrote for the majority, and Judges Southwick and Douglas dissented. The decision binds courts in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi, where many ICE detainees are held. The Supreme Court will address the related statutory question in Rhoney v. Barbosa da Cunha this term.
items.notes: The ruling came Oct 23 but was widely reported Oct 26 and was not in yesterday's brief. Just Security also lists a ruling that Trump unlawfully federalized California's National Guard for Los Angeles (MyNewsLA dates it Oct 23); I did not develop that.

items.text: The Energy Department is adding helium to its Critical Materials List in a notice published Oct 27, which opens federal support tools for supply-chain security. AIP's science-policy newsletter also reports that NASA is overhauling science-mission competitions, aiming to cut selection time from more than 30 months to about 19, and will not issue the annual ROSES research solicitation this year; the 2027 call is expected in January. The NSF's acting director and chief of staff plan to leave by year-end.
items.outlet: AIP FYI; Federal Register public inspection
items.notes: The helium notice (FR doc 2026-21884) is confirmed on the public-inspection list. The NASA and NSF items are single-sourced to AIP and their exact announcement dates are unclear.

items.text: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 in Game 3 of the World Series on Oct 26 in St. Petersburg, scoring eight runs in the fifth inning, and lead the series 3-0. Rookie Robert Gasser allowed one hit over six innings. Milwaukee can win its first-ever title in Game 4 on Oct 27.

Puck reported on Oct 25 that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wants Sen. Marsha Blackburn, the favourite in Tennessee's Nov 3 governor's race, to appoint him to her Senate seat if she wins. Hegseth has not confirmed the report. Critics frame it as a way out before a possible post-midterm House impeachment push.
items.notes: Secondhand: Puck's original is paywalled and unseen, and Daily Kos is left-leaning, so treat this as gossip until confirmed. Separately, the Pentagon's FORTRESS base-resilience office is due to be set up by Oct 30 (Newsweek).

items.text: PHMSA is publishing a 145-page proposed rule on Oct 27 that would align US hazardous-materials transport rules with international standards. The same day DHS is suspending the CNMI Economic Vitality and Security Travel Authorization Program for visitors to the Northern Mariana Islands, and the Coast Guard is imposing entry conditions on vessels arriving from Somalia.
items.notes: Based only on public-inspection titles (docs 2026-21922, 2026-21880, 2026-21865); I did not read the documents' content or comment deadlines.

items.text: Speaking at a press conference in Hanoi on Monday, PM Donald Tusk said of Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz's exit 'krzyż na drogę' (roughly, good riddance), and that everyone who had worked with her knew it was for the best. He said removing her from her party was not his decision. He said he would give the funds and regional policy ministry to a non-partisan expert he fully trusts, whose job is to finish the EU recovery fund (KPO) projects. He has two strong candidates, both women, and will name one after returning to Poland. He did not respond directly to Szymon Hołownia's demand that the post stay with Polska 2050. Sejm Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty (Lewica) said coalition partners should 'know their place' and that the PM should form the cabinet after consulting them.
items.notes: PAP via Bankier also carries Polska 2050 deputy chair Wioleta Tomczak, who said the party is relying on the 2023 coalition agreement being honoured; Hołownia would pull the ministers out but keep the club in the coalition. On the right, wPolityce headlined that Tusk is 'pinning a KPO affair' on her (article could not be fetched). Rzeczpospolita (Kolanko) mentions Elżbieta Bieńkowska as a possible candidate, unconfirmed.

items.text: The right-wing channel wPolsce24 aired a recording of Pełczyńska-Nałęcz speaking privately. In it she criticised the appointment of Maciej Berek, who went straight from government to the Constitutional Tribunal, as installing a politician. She also said he did not meet the formal criteria. She claimed Hołownia met Tusk several times without her knowledge to discuss replacing her. Separately, Unia Centrum MP Rafał Kasprzyk suggested on Polsat News that she rigged Polska 2050's internal leadership vote, but admitted he had no evidence.
items.notes: Recording is an excerpt published by a pro-PiS channel; its date and context are unknown. No response from Berek, Hołownia or Tusk was reported. Kasprzyk's claim is unsupported by his own admission.

items.text: An Ipsos poll for TVP Info (21–22 October, 1,000 adults) puts KO at 34%, PiS 26%, Konfederacja 10%, Grzegorz Braun's Korona 8%, Nowa Lewica 6%, PSL 5%, Rozwój Plus and Razem 4% each, and Polska 2050 at 1%. In a seat simulation, KO, Lewica and PSL would have 219 seats, short of the 231 majority, while PiS, Konfederacja and Korona would have 241.
items.notes: Single poll; fieldwork was right around Pełczyńska-Nałęcz's resignation. PSL's seat figure (5) looks low and is as reported.

items.text: The Senate budget and public finance committee backed amendments by Senator Kazimierz Kleina (KO) that would restore the government's version of the 2027 tax reform. They strike the Sejm's annual inflation indexation of PIT thresholds from 2028 and bring back the CIT rise from 19% to 22% for firms with revenue above €50m. Deputy Finance Minister Jurand Drop put the cost of indexation at about 4.1bn zł in 2028, 8.9bn zł in 2029 and 13.8bn zł in 2030. He warned that it could otherwise force cuts to tax reliefs or other tax rises. A legal news service (LEX) says the full Senate vote is set for Tuesday 27 October; any Senate amendments then go back to the Sejm.
items.notes: Committee vote count not reported. The Tuesday plenary date comes from LEX (undated page) and matches the Senate's scheduled 27 October sitting (Portal Samorządowy); no outlet gave a vote count. The Sejm can reject Senate amendments by absolute majority, and the Sejm itself added both changes against the government, so the final outcome is open. Not yet checked against a right-leaning outlet.

items.text: Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka set Tuesday's maximum retail fuel prices at 6.58 zł/l for 95 petrol, 7.27 zł for 98 and 8.18 zł for diesel. That is up from 6.51, 7.21 and 7.99 zł, a 19-grosz rise for diesel. The caps are the third phase of the 'Ceny Paliwa Niżej' package, which cuts fuel VAT and excise. It is funded by a 60% tax on fuel companies' above-normal profits from March 2026 to March 2027. The government expects the package to run to the end of 2026 at a cost of about 5bn zł. The President signed the law but referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review.
items.notes: Prices are set by daily ministerial announcement; the official notice was not fetched. The background (Iran-war oil shock, phases) is as reported by Polsat.

items.text: The Warsaw Stock Exchange recovered from Friday's falls. The WIG rose 0.86% to 158,712 points and the WIG20 0.74% to 4,198, led by banks: the WIG-Banki index was up 1.92%, with Pekao +2.0% and PKO BP +1.8%. Dino (−1.5%), Tauron, PGE and Orlen (−0.95%, on lower oil prices) fell.
items.notes: Złoty moves not reported.

items.text: During the first visit by a Polish PM to Vietnam in 16 years, Tusk and Prime Minister Lê Minh Hưng raised relations to a strategic partnership covering trade and investment, security and defence, and education and science. They signed agreements on scholarships (rising from 20 to 50) and on tourism. They also set up a joint trade and investment committee with a target of $6bn in mutual investment by 2030. Deputy state assets minister Konrad Gołota said talks are under way on Vietnamese purchases of Krab howitzers and Rosomak vehicles. LOT plans direct Warsaw–Hanoi flights from Q1 2027. Tusk said Poland's priority is a better trade balance, and he acknowledged differences over Russia's war in Ukraine.
items.notes: WNP says no defence deal was signed. A Wprost business headline says the first contracts (Rosomak, Krab, ammunition) could come this year (not fetched). Vietnam will 'consider' visa-free travel for Poles.

items.text: Opening the 4th Polish-German Economic Forum in Warsaw (organised by PAIH), Finance and Economy Minister Andrzej Domański told German participants that under no scenario would there be a return to 'business as usual' with Russia. He said Poland will never agree to resume imports of Russian raw materials, including gas. He called for deregulation, a competitive EU energy market and European advantages in critical raw materials, and said economic strength must go together with security.
items.notes: Coverage frames it as a warning to Germany; the article did not describe any specific German proposal prompting it. The rp.pl link was not opened.

items.text: Health Minister Jolanta Sobierańska-Grenda reacted to Polsat's investigation into doctors' pay, in which only 19 of 590 hospitals answered questions. She said the pay-reporting rules in force since 1 July will give a true picture, and that hospital directors are responsible for wages. She proposed capping wages at 65% of a hospital's spending, following AOTMiT advice. At the Forum Rynku Zdrowia she said the 2027 NFZ budget could be about 16bn zł short despite record health spending of 274bn zł. Debate there focused on a reform package that extends the hospital network to mid-2029 and gives the NFZ power to bar doctors from NFZ-funded work for misconduct. The President's Health Council chair, Prof. Piotr Czauderna, criticised the package.
items.notes: The 65% cap is a proposal, not a decision. The reform package awaits the Senate and President; the minister said she hopes they approve it.

items.text: FM Radosław Sikorski asked on X who was prompting President Karol Nawrocki to call the Russian threat a sham. This followed a Rzeczpospolita interview in which Nawrocki said he saw no drastic change in the Russian threat and accused the government of 'distributing fear'. Sikorski told CNN that Russia is waging a hybrid war just below the threshold of open invasion, including sabotage, arson and airspace violations. In a separate YouTube interview, Nawrocki said communication with Tusk works despite deep disagreements, and that the two have held unpublicised crisis-scenario exercises.
items.notes: The Rzeczpospolita interview was not read directly; Nawrocki's quote is from Goniec's account. Sikorski's paraphrase ('ściema') is his characterisation, not Nawrocki's word.

items.text: Seven armed police officers raided the Warsaw flat of Bartosz Malewski, head of the Independence March association and lawyer for Piotr W. (detained at the 16 October Constitutional Tribunal protest), after an online post falsely reported a murder there. Police have opened a case over the false report. Malewski called it a malicious 'swatting', did not rule out a Russian or Belarusian provocation, and said the 11 November march will go ahead.
items.notes: The motive suggestions are Malewski's own.

items.text: Gazeta Wyborcza obtained a 2018 letter from then-Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro to PM Morawiecki backing an interministerial team on crypto regulation and warning of fraud and money-laundering risks. The letter undercuts Ziobro's claim that he knew little about cryptocurrencies when his foundation accepted 450,000 zł in autumn 2025 from Zondacrypto chief Przemysław Kral. Ziobro admits he failed to vet Kral. The exchange went bankrupt in 2026 with estimated client losses of 170m zł.
items.notes: No formal charges are reported over the donation. Liberal-outlet sourcing (Wyborcza); no right-leaning response was read.

items.text: EU Consumer Credit Directive 2 (2023/2225) must be applied from 20 November 2026. It brings many buy-now-pay-later and small loans under full consumer-credit rules, with stricter creditworthiness checks, advertising warnings and rights over automated decisions. Poland has missed the November 2025 transposition deadline and has no implementing law. In May the PM withdrew UOKiK's mandate to run the draft (UC82). Wprost reports that Poland will not be ready in time.
items.notes: The Wprost article could not be fetched (headline only). The legislative status comes from Homebanking.pl, verified as of 7 August 2026, so any later government adoption may be missing.

items.text: An SW Research poll for Rzeczpospolita found 67.2% of Poles want the abortion law liberalised. Of these, 37.7% back abortion on demand to 12 weeks and 29.5% want a return to the pre-2020 compromise; 16.2% want the current law kept and 6% want it tightened. Support is higher among women (73.8%) than men (60.3%). The two bills passed by the Sejm await the Senate and an expected presidential veto.
items.outlet: Notes from Poland (SW Research for Rzeczpospolita)
items.notes: No Senate date for the abortion bills was found.

items.text: On 26 October, Mayor Łukasz Gibała's order No. 2251/2026 appeared in the city's Public Information Bulletin (BIP). The order sets new organisational rules for City Hall and abolishes its six departments. It took effect when he signed it on 23 October, apart from a new Health Office, which starts on 1 December. The city told PAP the change saves about 2.3 million zł a year; Kraków has debts of about 9 billion zł and a gap of roughly 390 million zł in this year's current spending. Under the new division of duties, deputy mayor Jan Hoffman oversees ZTP (public transport), ZDMK (roads), municipal companies and culture. Elżbieta Kois-Żurek oversees education, housing, social welfare and health, and first deputy Karol Wałachowski oversees metro preparation, planning, sport and the environment. Gibała also abolished the posts of pupils' ombudsman and violence-prevention ombudsman, and created a new plenipotentiary for breaches of the law.
items.outlet: Radio Kraków; KRKnews; PAP via Bankier
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: The 2.3 million zł savings figure comes from City Hall, via PAP/Bankier. LoveKraków, citing anonymous sources close to the mayor, says the division of duties is temporary and that the dismissed directors will probably not get other posts. IKC quotes a former director who learned of his dismissal in a brief hallway conversation. The sources disagree on detail: LoveKraków puts tourism and investment under Wałachowski, while KRKnews lists municipal investments under Hoffman. No on-record reaction from the opposition (KO) was found.

items.text: At its session on 26 October, the Małopolska regional assembly (sejmik) unanimously adopted an appeal to the Lviv Oblast Council. It asks the council to withdraw its decision to make 2027 the Year of the UPA, Roman Shukhevych and Oleh Olzhych. The appeal says the decision conflicts with the two regions' 2004 cooperation declaration and dishonours victims of the UPA's crimes, but it does not suspend cooperation. On the same day, the Lublin assembly voted to end its cooperation with Lviv Oblast, and Podkarpackie condemned the Lviv decision. Kraków's own draft resolution suspending its city partnership with Lviv is still waiting for the City Council; no reply from Lviv was reported.
items.thread: Kraków–Lviv partnership and the Year of the UPA
items.notes: The detail on Lublin and Podkarpackie comes from Portal Samorządowy headlines and NCZAS; I did not read the full articles. On 27 October LoveKraków re-reported Gibała's letter to Lviv mayor Andriy Sadovyi, but other outlets date that letter to 21 October, so it is not new.

items.text: The Małopolska voivode has granted a building permit for a shooting-range complex for the University of the National Education Commission (UKEN) at the historic Bronowice fort. The permit was issued under a special statute, so it bypasses local zoning plans and public consultation. Radio Kraków reported on 26 October that the site has been handed to the contractor. Residents, who fear damage to the fort and to green space, say they will appeal within a week and will write to the Kraków Rectors' Conference.
items.notes: Radio Kraków says the appeal goes to the Minister of Finance, which looks unusual and may be an error in that report. The project's cost and funding were not reported.

items.text: GDDKiA showed journalists the Mistrzejowice junction and the S7 viaducts in Kraków on 26 October. Around noon on Thursday 29 October, the full Mistrzejowice II roundabout linking ul. Okulickiego and ul. Petöfiego should open, moving local traffic to the lower level. The viaducts carrying S7 through Nowa Huta towards Warsaw are due to open at the end of October, probably on 30 or 31 October, with temporary traffic arrangements and a speed limit. The direct link from S7 to the northern bypass (S52) is not expected until late November or early December.
items.notes: The 30/31 October date for the viaducts is LoveKraków's estimate; GDDKiA has given no exact date. I could not open the Gazeta Krakowska piece and saw only its summary.

items.text: Cracovia has parted ways with its sporting director, Filip Trubalski, after weekend protests by fans following the 3:1 loss at Piast Gliwice. Mirosław Hajdo has been named director of the club's Rącz training centre. In an interview, Trubalski denied blocking a fan visit to a training session before the derby.
items.notes: Based on Nasze Miasto's press-review summaries of the two Gazeta Krakowska articles; I could not open the articles themselves.

items.text: Carlos Santana will play TAURON Arena Kraków on 24 July 2027 as part of his Planet of Free Will Global Tour. Fan-club presales open at 12:00 on 27 October, and general sale starts at 12:00 on 30 October via Live Nation.

Kraków police report that a 33-year-old man stole a client's Lexus in Kraków and set it on fire in Zielonki. He also damaged a police car and had drugs on him. He faces six charges, and a court ordered three months' pre-trial detention.
items.notes: Taken from the police news listing and outlet headlines; I could not open the full police release.

items.text: BJP workers protested on October 26 in several state capitals, including Gandhinagar, Guwahati, Shimla, Jaipur, Lucknow and Kolkata, over Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's 'Modi ka baap bhi jayega' remark in Patna. Police stopped marches toward Congress offices in Gujarat and Rajasthan, and protesters scuffled with police in Shimla while trying to burn an effigy. Kharge has not apologised. Ashok Gehlot said the words are an ordinary Hindi idiom being misread, and the Quint reports that Congress says Kharge meant Modi's 'ideological parent', the RSS. On October 27 West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari said the language reflected the style of Sonia and Rahul Gandhi.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: No Swarajya or Scroll piece on this found. The Week and the Quint report the Congress defence (idiom; a BJP worker had insulted Kharge's late father; the target was the RSS). Republic Bharat (Hindi, pro-BJP) carries only BJP criticism. Outlook says BJP worker Krishna Kumar Singh filed a complaint at Patna Kotwali police station on Oct 25, to be moved to Gandhi Maidan PS. No FIR has been reported.

items.text: The Election Commission filed a short counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court in Rakesh Kumar Singh v. Union of India, a plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. It says all three SIR orders (June 2025, October 2025, May 2026) were unanimous decisions of the full Commission, and that individual commissioners' file notes are not decisions. It also says Form 6 was not amended, conceding that the online display could give that impression, and argues the CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge. The petition rests on one Indian Express report that the two Election Commissioners objected 14 times. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Bagchi and Mohana listed the matter for October 27.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Framing differs. Organiser (RSS-linked) headlines 'EC hits back' and gives the rebuttal most space. Scroll sets the EC's unanimity claim against the Indian Express report of 14 objections. It also notes that the online Form 6 cannot be submitted without the new SIR declaration, and that BJP-ruled states have used SIR deletions to deny ration cards. Business Today also says an IIT/IISc expert committee will review ECINet.

items.text: Indian shares recovered from early losses on October 26 to end a four-session losing streak. Sensex closed up 483 points (0.66%) at 73,606.75 and Nifty up 153 points at 22,753.20, led by metals, pharma and oil and gas stocks. The rupee fell 25 paise to 95.19 per dollar, with Brent near $114.50 after touching about $117. Traders told Business Recorder the RBI sold dollars around 95.30. Early on October 27 the indices were roughly flat, with IT stocks weighing and defence stocks rallying after the DAC approvals.
items.notes: Yesterday's brief reported the weak open; the day ended higher. Business Standard's headline gives Nifty as 23,753, a typo for 22,753. Aaj Tak (Hindi) puts 2026 FPI outflows at about Rs 4.5 lakh crore, roughly Rs 51,000 crore of it in October. The RBI intervention detail comes from unnamed traders (Business Recorder/Reuters).

items.text: Shares in the Jio Platforms IPO, a fresh issue of up to Rs 30,213 crore at Rs 1,065–1,119 a share, were allotted on October 26, with listing on NSE and BSE set for October 28. Per IPO Watch, the issue was subscribed 21.36 times overall: 67 times in the institutional portion and 2.76 times in the retail portion. Grey-market premiums were about Rs 250 after the issue closed.
items.notes: Subscription figures come from IPO aggregators, not checked against NSE/BSE data. Issue size and dates are from Groww's pre-issue note, and the dates were 'tentative'. GMP is unofficial.

items.text: Shares of eMudhra fell up to 10% to a 52-week low of Rs 318 on October 26. That is down 43% in five sessions since the company disclosed that eight of its intermediate certificate-authority keys were weak and exited the global SSL/TLS business. Business Standard reports that Google will remove the emSign ECC Root CA – G3 from the Chrome Root Store from October 27. MeitY's special investigating team has not yet reported. Officials say CCA-regulated digital signatures and eSign are unaffected.
items.notes: MediaNama (Oct 23) argues that the exit is not enough and that the CCA has issued no public statement. ICRA has kept its rating but flags reputational risk. No new MeitY findings were published.

items.text: The Defence Acquisition Council, chaired by Rajnath Singh, gave Acceptance of Necessity on October 26 to capital procurement proposals worth about Rs 2.12 lakh crore, about 82% to be sourced from Indian industry. The Army list includes self-propelled tracked guns, light multi-role helicopters, VSHORAD air defence, counter-drone systems, surveillance UAVs and long-range kamikaze drones. The Navy gets offboard decoy systems against anti-ship missiles, and the IAF helicopters, air defence systems and X-band weather radars. AoN is an in-principle clearance, not a contract.
items.notes: PIB release not retrieved. Figures are widely reported from the MoD statement. Defence stocks rose up to 9% on Oct 27 (Business Standard).

items.text: Five people were shot dead and one wounded at a hotel in Guwahati around 9 pm on October 26. Police arrested the property's leaseholder, Ghanakanta Gogoi, within an hour and seized the weapon. Police Commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said a lease dispute is the suspected motive. Four victims were from one family linked to the hotel owner. Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi demanded that CM Himanta Biswa Sarma take responsibility for law and order.
items.notes: Reports differ on the location: The Week says Hotel Bilas Inn, Bora Service, while PTI/ANI say the Ulubari area.

items.text: Cyclone Arnab became a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal. IMD expects it to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm (115–125 km/h, gusts to 140) and cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28. Andhra Pradesh has put 16 districts on alert, readied 1,763 shelters and is evacuating about 89,000 people. Fishing is suspended and coastal roads close from the afternoon of October 27. Odisha expects very heavy rain from October 27 to 30, and schools in five southern districts close on October 28–29.
items.notes: IMD bulletins could not be fetched (robots). Details come from ANI/APSDMA and National Herald, and the Odisha details from a Vajiram & Ravi summary. National Herald already calls it 'very severe', whereas ANI says it is expected to become so.

items.text: About 4,000 Indians, mostly Umrah pilgrims, remain stranded in Saudi Arabia, according to ETV Bharat. Air India and Air India Express have suspended Riyadh and Dammam flights until November 7 and Jeddah flights until October 31. Families report extra costs of Rs 4,000–5,000 per person a day and fares of up to Rs 50,000, and some pilgrims are driving to Dubai, Qatar or Oman to fly home. Madhya Pradesh minister Krishna Gaur is reportedly writing to the MEA. No Centre-run special flights have been announced.
items.notes: Air India dates are from one Hindi regional report (reporter Syed Abid) and not checked against the airline. The 4,000 figure matches Owaisi/MEA reporting of Oct 23. MEA said on Oct 22 that about 3,000 had already returned.

items.text: Liechtenstein's Hereditary Prince Alois, on the first state visit by Liechtenstein to India, arrived in New Delhi from Vadodara on October 26 with Princess Sofia and a business delegation. MoS Jayant Singh received him. Talks with PM Modi at Hyderabad House on October 27 are to cover trade, investment, science, technology and innovation, along with meetings with Jaishankar, Sitharaman and President Murmu. The MEA links the visit to the India–EFTA TEPA, which took effect in 2025.
items.notes: No outcomes of the talks were reported at time of writing.

items.text: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal visited the Netherlands on October 25–27 after Berlin. He met trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma and economy minister Heleen Herbert and co-chaired an India–Netherlands Business Forum on opportunities under the concluded India–EU FTA. In The Hague on October 27 he said the EU, UK and EFTA pacts would bring investment, technology and jobs, especially in labour-intensive sectors. On October 22 he said the EU deal could be signed before year-end and take effect in four to five months. No agreements were signed on the trip.
items.notes: The signing timeline is Goyal's own claim (ANI, Oct 22) and has no EU confirmation.

items.text: Protests resumed at Jamia Millia Islamia on October 26 after the university's order promising students' union elections within 15 days of a union constitution being approved. About 100 women students gathered near Gate 7 and several were detained by Delhi Police. Students want a fixed election date and a chief election officer. JMISU has not held elections since 2006.

Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said in Belagavi on October 26 that he will talk to sugarcane growers before meeting mill owners, after farmers blocked a state highway at Gurlapur on October 25 demanding a Rs 1,000-per-tonne incentive. He said some mills have not paid the extra Rs 250 a tonne the state had asked for, and that the Centre bears 90% of the responsibility. He has sought a meeting with Union minister Pralhad Joshi.

ISRO plans to launch the NVS-03 navigation satellite on a GSLV (F18) from Sriharikota at 11:51 pm IST on October 30. It is the third of five second-generation NavIC satellites. NVS-02 failed to reach its orbit in 2025, leaving NavIC with only three satellites providing services. NVS-03 is meant to restore independent positioning after in-orbit testing.
items.notes: No ISRO press release retrieved. Both sources are secondary.

items.text: The men's hockey Asian Champions Trophy begins on October 27 in Jalandhar, Punjab, with India, the defending champions, opening against Bangladesh. The semi-finals and final are in Mohali. Bangladesh replaced Pakistan, which withdrew. It is the first time the event has been held in Punjab in 17 years.
items.notes: Reporter Abhishek Mishra. The reason for Pakistan's withdrawal is not given.
